title: Worldwide specialist shops — wave two strict-gate research
status: 15 high-confidence rows imported as drafts pending human editorial promotion.

import.warning: Draft import is not human editorial approval. Recheck current trading hours before travel; do not re-import these rows.

method.editorial_contract: A currently trading, independently visitable physical storefront whose deep narrow inventory or living trade is itself worth a walking detour.
method.category_rule: Existing categories win for books, records, food, bakeries and wine; specialistshops is reserved for otherwise-unrepresented trades and collections.
method.exclusions: Chains, malls, department stores, ordinary antiques, appointment-only dealers, museum shops, concept stores, multi-location businesses and storefronts without first-party current evidence.
method.source_policy: At least two useful sources per include: a current first-party shop/contact page plus dated recent status corroboration and, where separate, a history/inventory source.
method.coordinate_policy: Named map object, government exact-address point or first-party map coordinate tied to the current physical address.
method.dedupe_policy: Normalised names and every listed alias checked globally against 17,131 live rows and earlier dossier candidates. Global proximity at 120 m triggers manual identity/address review.
method.editorial_gate: At least 19/25 overall, with story and walkability each at least 4/5; all confidence dimensions high; stop below target rather than pad.
method.import_policy: All rows remain draft-only and require quality flag d if later imported.

missing_city_requirements.rule: Historical proposal provenance. Regensburg and Montville were added through the reviewed discovery-wave-2 city plan before draft import.

included.s: seven hundred shelves of paper and the tools to bind it
included.w: What began as a bookbinders' supply shop in 1988 now fills 700 shelves with fine papers from around the world, backed by walls of bookcloth, leather and hand tools. This is the public retail shop—not the appointment-only bindery—and it rewards slow material browsing.
facts: The public paper and bookbinding shop began in 1988.
Its Gillingham Street shop contains 700 shelves of paper plus bookcloth, leather and specialist tools.
The first-party contact page posts walk-in hours Monday to Saturday.

included.s: sixty years of tricks demonstrated across a Clerkenwell counter
included.w: A family magic shop has worked from this Clerkenwell address for more than sixty years, carrying a dense stock of cards, coins, stage apparatus and teaching material for beginners and professionals. The real pleasure is the living counter culture: ask, watch and learn how a trick is sold.
facts: The family business has operated from 89 Clerkenwell Road for more than 60 years.
The shop carries a large stock spanning close-up, mentalism, stage and beginner magic.
Its current site posts public opening hours Tuesday to Saturday.

included.s: three floors of hats above an untouched 1886 counter
included.q: Casa Yustas Plaza Mayor Madrid Spain
included.w: Casa Yustas has sold hats on Plaza Mayor since 1886, retaining a protected chestnut interior while an upstairs workshop shapes caps, ceremonial headwear and bespoke pieces. It is both a working trade and one of the square's rare reasons to go indoors.
facts: The business has traded on Plaza Mayor since 1886.
Its protected original interior is fitted in chestnut wood.
The shop spans three floors and maintains an in-house workshop for hats, caps and custom work.

included.s: Taiwan's last working foundry for traditional Chinese metal type

Its Japanese candles use plant materials including scarce haze-tree wax.
